column3: The Hebrew says to “cut a covenant” and explicitly names Nahash as the recipient of the men’s words. BSB uses “Make a treaty” and refers to him as “him.”
The Hebrew says “we will come out to you”; BSB makes the submission explicit with “we will surrender to you.”
The Hebrew says they spoke “in the ears of the people,” then that the people lifted their voice and wept. BSB uses “in the hearing” and “wept aloud.”
The Hebrew says Saul was coming from the field behind the cattle; BSB explicitly makes this a return and supplies the possessive “his oxen.”
The Hebrew describes his anger through the image of his nose burning; BSB renders this as burning “with great anger.”
The Hebrew says the pieces were sent “by the hand of the messengers”; BSB leaves the hand image implicit.
The Hebrew leaves the one numbering unnamed and uses collective singular “man of Judah.” BSB supplies Saul and uses plural “men of Judah.”
The Hebrew says “we will come out to you” and describes what is “good in your eyes.” BSB supplies Nahash as the addressee and leaves both “to you” and the eyes image implicit.

The Hebrew calls the divisions “three heads” and names Ammon collectively; BSB has “three divisions” and “the Ammonites.” It says until the heat of the day, without an explicit superlative corresponding to “hottest.”
The Hebrew quotes the dissenting words as “Shall Saul reign over us?” without an explicit negative. BSB adds “not” in “Saul should not reign over us.”
The Hebrew introduces Saul’s words with the general “said”; BSB specifies that he “ordered.”

The Hebrew twice names Gilgal and twice uses “there” for the sacrificing and rejoicing; BSB names Gilgal once and uses “There” once. It describes making Saul king, where BSB says they “confirmed” him as king.
